$comment: The closed vocabulary. A role may only emit properties from `properties` and only name tokens that exist in the adapter or literals from `keywords`. Anything else is an error at check time, which is what makes 'zero-bloat' a gate instead of a promise.
$stateSelectorsNote: Allowed nested selectors, AND the cascade contract. Almost every state selector has the same specificity, so source order decides which wins when two of them set the same property - and source order here is this array's order. Read it as priority: a state later in the list beats an earlier one. That is why `:active` comes after `:hover` (a pressed control must not fall back to its hover look) and why every `[data-*]` state comes after the pseudo-classes (library state outranks pointer state). The alternative - `!important`, or nesting tricks - would put the decision inside the emitter instead of inside this file, which is the one thing CORE-IDEA.md forbids. A few entries are descendant selectors like `[data-state="checked"] &`, which style a part from an ancestor's state (bits-ui puts `data-state` on both the switch root and its thumb); those carry more specificity, so they win outright and never tie.
